newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says no case against Megawati's rival.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says no case against Megawati's rival.

text.p: Indonesian police say there is no evidence to link the government-backed rival of ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader Megawati Sukarnoputri with riots in Jakarta in July, the Antara news agency said on Friday.

Jakarta police chief Major-General Hamami Nata was quoted as saying he had found no evidence to charge the PDI's new chief, Surjadi, with inciting the July 27 riots, the worst in the city for more than 20 years in which at least five people died.
"We have questioned him but we have not found enough evidence to build a case against him," Nata was quoted as saying by the official news agency.
Surjadi, who is also deputy parliamentary speaker, replaced Megawati as leader of the minority PDI in June this year at a government-backed rebel party congress.
Megawati, daughter of late founding president Sukarno, says the move was illegal as she had been elected to a five-year term as PDI chairman in 1993.
Rioting erupted after Surjadi supporters backed by police raided PDI's headquarters in Jakarta which had been occupied by Megawati loyalists since the rebel congress.
The National Commission on Human Rights criticised the government for arresting only PDI supporters loyal to Megawati.
Earlier this week, 115 Megawati loyalists charged with disobeying police orders and refusing to disperse at PDI headquarters were freed after serving four months in jail.
As yet no proceedings have been taken against Surjadi supporters.
Political analysts say the government wanted to replace Megawati as PDI leader for fear she might attract votes away from the ruling Golkar in general elections to be held next May.
